messages.content: Get the latest closing prices and volumes for Apple Inc., Google LLC., and Microsoft Corporation in the New York Stock Exchange

function.name: get_stock_data
function.description: Retrieve the most recent trading day's closing price and volume for a specified stock. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

symbol.description: The stock symbol of the company.

data_points.description: The type of data you want to retrieve for the stock. This can include closing price, opening price, volume, etc.

message.reasoning:
The user wants the latest closing prices and volumes for Apple Inc., Google LLC., and Microsoft Corporation in the NYSE. Actually Apple (AAPL) is on NASDAQ, not NYSE; Google (Alphabet) is also on NASDAQ; Microsoft (MSFT) is on Nasdaq too. But maybe they just want the latest closing prices and volumes for those companies. We need to use the function get_stock_data. The function signature expects symbol and data_points which can be "price" or "volume". It says data_points: "price" | "volume"[] - unclear if it's an array? Probably we pass ["price", "volume"].

We need to call the function three times: one for each symbol. Or maybe we can combine? The function only accepts one symbol at a time. So we need to call it separately for AAPL, GOOG, MSFT. We'll do separate calls. Then we will format the results nicely.

We'll call get_stock_data with symbol="AAPL", data_points=["price","volume"]. Then same for GOOG and MSFT. We'll then present the results.
